purpose: Persistent local Bazaar with PostgreSQL, Redis and existing background job groups managed together. This is the isolated local UI fixture, not a customer or production database.

commands.behavior: Start waits for authenticated database/Redis/migration health, then exits successfully. The supervisor and services remain in the background after closing the terminal. Repeating start is safe; changed source/configuration triggers a backed-up restart and a build when necessary.
commands.afterReboot: Run pnpm local again. No macOS boot agent was installed.
commands.development: Existing pnpm dev/start and database scripts retain their meanings. Use pnpm local for this managed stack. Do not run prepare/seed/reset to restart it.

prerequisites.verifiedHost: macOS with existing Node, pnpm, PostgreSQL 16 and Redis binaries
prerequisites.installation: No automatic software installation; missing binaries produce an explicit error. Homebrew Apple Silicon/Intel paths and PATH are checked.
prerequisites.build: First start or changed application sources requires a production build. Unchanged subsequent starts use the verified private app copy.

services.supervision: Readiness and ownership checks, 2-second monitoring, application/database/Redis crash recovery. Foreign listeners are not terminated or adopted.
services.control: Private authenticated Unix socket. An unauthenticated stop attempt returned 403 and left the supervisor running.

jobs.verification: Existing recovery and email endpoints returned HTTP 200. Per-group in-flight guards prevent overlap. No new business job implementation was added.

storage.uploads: Private app public/uploads and uploads link to persistent files/public-uploads and files/uploads.
storage.exports: Private app tmp and TMPDIR/TMP/TEMP use persistent files/tmp.
storage.identity: Stable private manifest secrets preserve local sign-in sessions across ordinary stack restarts; data and backup roots use mode 0700, manifest mode 0600.
storage.isolation: Ignored by Git, TypeScript/Vitest scanning, formatting and Next standalone output tracing. App dependencies resolve inside its private copy, independent of .next build-cache cleanup.
storage.durability: PostgreSQL fsync, synchronous_commit and full_page_writes verified on. Dedicated Redis uses AOF with appendfsync always and RDB snapshots.
storage.adoption: Recovered legacy cluster was backed up, stopped cleanly and copied once. All rows across 132 tables matched. Original cluster/dump retained. Existing uploads are copied without overwriting differing files; legacy Redis DB4 migration copied 0 keys.
storage.missingData: Initialization/adoption markers refuse automatic empty recreation or stale legacy reuse when existing managed data is missing. Recovery must be explicit. No seed, db push or reset runs during startup; pending migrations use prisma migrate deploy after a backup.

backups.schedule: Before startup migrations, after persistent app files are ready, every 30 minutes while the supervisor runs, on manual request and during controlled shutdown.
backups.database: Unique custom-format pg_dump files; shutdown snapshot follows stopping the application.
backups.files: Per-snapshot .dump.files.json manifests and SHA256-addressed immutable objects. Identical bytes are stored once; earlier versions remain restorable.
backups.retention: No automatic pruning or deletion. Monitor capacity with local:status/logs and ordinary disk tools.
backups.spaceGuards: Minimum 512 MiB reserve during normal operation, 3 GiB before a build, plus estimated database/file-copy requirements before writing backups. Low space produces an explicit blocked state; existing data and backups are not deleted to make room.
backups.restoreVerification: Shutdown dump restored into a separate disposable database with all 132 table hashes equal. File snapshots restored with hash/size checks and Redis RDB restored in a separate temporary Redis instance.
backups.restorePolicy: No automatic destructive restore command. Keep the current directory intact; restore a chosen dump into a separate database and verify before any deliberate replacement. File restore helper refuses path escapes, corrupted objects and overwriting different existing content.

dataIncident.priorFailure: The previous temporary cluster lost internal files at midnight on 2026-10-27. The deleting process was not established. Its broken directory remains untouched.
dataIncident.historicalLoss: Recovery used the 2026-10-26 07:29 Bishkek snapshot: 472 business rows across 11 tracked models. Thirteen synthetic QA rows created later remain absent; this work does not claim to recover them. Historical 485-row acceptance evidence describes the earlier dataset.
dataIncident.currentPreservation: All 472 recovered business rows still match the before-adoption dump by model row hashes after the new runtime, crash and restore checks. No customer or production database was used.

faultChecks.boundary: Explicit isolated fixture/organization checks; unique disposable verification databases and Redis test keys. External providers disabled throughout.

browser.result: Real fresh admin login and dashboard read passed on canonical localhost:3122 in IAB. Session survived the final stack restart.
browser.limit: Existing Chrome tab automation timed out; successful login/restart evidence is IAB, not a claimed Chrome-specific acceptance.

correctionsDuringImplementation: Fixed initial PostgreSQL/Redis readiness timing before dependent commands.
Fixed process ownership checks to use actual cwd and listener ownership: Next changes process.title, making a ps command-name check unreliable.

Initial whole-file backup duplication filled local disk during repeated verification. Replaced it with content-addressed snapshots; all 16 existing file snapshot versions were converted and independently restored/hash-checked before obsolete tar representations were removed. Backup footprint fell from about 2.4 GB to about 122 MB at conversion. Reproducible .next/cache and an incomplete verification copy were also removed; no database or logical backup version was discarded. Final complete verification passed after these fixes.

providers.normalManualUse: Existing local AI configuration including DeepSeek is available to the user; the key was not changed or committed.
providers.automatedTests: AI/provider calls disabled. No actual AI, acquiring, marketplace or external mail request was made by these checks.
providers.otherIntegrations: Local payment collection disabled, email log-only, marketplace credentials isolated. This task verifies the local infrastructure, not live external integration quality.
providers.handoffApproval: Initial normal-mode handoff was rejected by automatic approval review because AI settings could allow real requests. Read-only proof confirmed no pending AI jobs and all automated checks complete; the explicit manual-use handoff was then approved. Evidence: artifacts/ux/espresso/local-runtime-handoff-provider-boundary.json.

limits: Backups are on the same computer. This protects ordinary restart/crash workflows, not hardware loss or deliberate deletion of all copies. Off-device backups are not configured.

A live periodic database/file/Redis snapshot is not a single distributed transaction. Controlled shutdown backup and separate restore equality were tested; no cross-service point-in-time recovery claim is made.
No macOS boot auto-start or supervisor-of-supervisor was installed. If the supervisor itself is killed or the machine reboots, pnpm local recovers the managed stack.
Low disk capacity needs operator attention; backups are never silently pruned.
Native-host checks were run on this macOS environment; other operating systems are not certified by this delivery.

delivery.running: ready; database up, migrations ok, Redis up

followups.note: Later UI improvements rebuilt the same persistent runtime; a manual draft predating that task raises its preserved business baseline to473. Earlier472-row verification remains point-in-time evidence.
